core.text: Hypothesis: the mutable row-to-key interface carries the wrong-target effect. Preserve P1 refresh, snapshot loading and sorting, and P2 target selection and status commits. Ablate only the retained row association across refresh: capture the intended immutable key at selection and commit that key despite row reordering. The available key-bound replay supplies this interface intervention; neither parent is deleted.

Propose identical initial states and nine-minute schedules in row-bound and key-bound arms: select K2 at 0-1, refresh at 1-2, commit at 2-3; select K5 at 3-4, refresh at 4-5, commit at 5-6; select K7 at 6-7, refresh at 7-8, commit at 8-9. Predict row-bound writes K5, K7, K7, versus key-bound writes K2, K5, K7. Both retain three refreshes, source scores and final S2. Only the latter is predicted to attain the exact status map without an incorrect-key write. Log every action, loaded snapshot, selected row, intended key, actual write and final status. These are prospective model predictions, not executed outcomes.

residue.text: Retain the equal-score anomaly: S2 assigns 75 to both K5 and K7. Score cannot replace immutable identity; inspect keys and compare intended and actual written keys. A correct final map cannot erase an earlier incorrect-key write.

O5 supplies one synthetic miswrite, while repeated mismatch-triggered feedback remains unobserved. The primary matched schedule isolates the selection interface before adding response-driven refreshes. Separately logging refresh requests could investigate recurrence, but no recurrence or successful correction is established here. Real binding, detection costs and behavior under concurrent changes, deletion or load failure remain unknown; absent production resources prevent operational or human-benefit claims.

tension.account_a: Interface-mediated account: refresh causes a wrong-target write only when mutable row identity crosses into the status commit.
tension.account_b: Interface-independent account: refresh intrinsically causes the same wrong-target writes even when selection remains bound to the intended immutable key.
tension.prediction_a: With identical refreshes and action times, changing only binding predicts K5/K7/K7 in the row arm and K2/K5/K7 in the key arm; disappearance of miswrites supports interface mediation within the model.
tension.prediction_b: The same intervention predicts persistent K5/K7/K7 miswrites in both arms; persistence despite verified immutable-key binding contradicts the proposed sufficient interface mechanism.
